title: Generic etale-radicial factorization of a finite locally free scheme
statement:
Let $R$ be a nonzero Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $p:E\to S$ be finite locally free [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-finite-locally-free]. There exist $0\ne f\in R$ and an affine scheme $T$ with a factorization
$$E\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]\xrightarrow{u}T\xrightarrow{e}\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]$$
of the restriction of $p$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-ring-localization-away], such that $e$ is finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism], and $u$ is finite locally free and a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. In particular every base change of $u$ is bijective on underlying points. No reducedness or irreducibility of $E$ and no positive-rank assumption are imposed; when $E=\varnothing$ one may take $T=\varnothing$.

source.place: BLR 7.6 proof of Proposition 5(a), printed p.197 (PDF p.203), generic algebra K prime, maximal etale subalgebra L, and shrinking to etale/radicial factors. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. The finite local freeness of u is obtained by spreading its generic finite-dimensional L-module bases; this necessary strengthening is explicit here.

proof.text: Write $E=\operatorname{Spec}A$: this is possible because $p$ is finite, and $A$ is a finite $R$-module by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A finite module generating family also generates the algebra, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $A$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $B=A\otimes_RK$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $E_K$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B$; tensoring a finite generating family shows that $B$ is finite-dimensional over $K$. If $A=0$, take $f=1$ and $T=\varnothing$, with both maps the empty maps. The zero algebra is free with empty basis, hence these maps have the asserted finite local freeness by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum]; the empty map to the base is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-product], and the empty identity is a universal homeomorphism. Henceforth allow $B=0$ as well; all products below admit the empty index set.

source.place: Tags 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), 00U2(11) (lemma-etale); affine finite-module reduction; empty case

proof.text: Let $C=B_K(B)$ be the directed union of finite etale $K$-subalgebras supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-etale-subalgebra-directed-union]. It is a $K$-vector subspace of the finite-dimensional space $B$. Choose a finite $K$-basis of $C$. The finite-subset assertion of that node puts this basis in one finite etale subalgebra $D\subseteq C$. Since $D$ contains every $K$-linear combination of the basis, $C=D$; thus $C$ itself is finite etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], $C\cong\prod_jL_j$ for finite separable extensions $L_j/K$. Write $\epsilon_j$ for the corresponding orthogonal idempotents in $B$. The map $B\to\prod_j\epsilon_jB$, $b\mapsto(\epsilon_jb)_j$, has inverse $(b_j)\mapsto\sum_jb_j$. Each $\epsilon_jB$ has a finite basis over $L_j$: a finite $K$-spanning family is already an $L_j$-spanning family. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum] its spectrum is finite locally free over $\operatorname{Spec}L_j$. On the disjoint affine components of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ these are exactly the restrictions of $v:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, so $v$ is finite locally free. This only uses locality in the defining conditions [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tags 0CKR/0CKS (lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field, lemma-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra); algebra.tex Tag 00U3; morphisms.tex Tag 02KB

proof.text: Fix any algebraically closed extension field $\Omega/K$. By [lem-sfb-maximal-ind-etale-field-base-change], $C\otimes_K\Omega=B_\Omega(B\otimes_K\Omega)$. Set $H=B\otimes_K\Omega$. This finite-dimensional algebra is Artinian: a strict descending chain of ideals is a strict descending chain of finite-dimensional vector subspaces, so has length at most $\dim_\Omega H$. Apply [lem-sfb-artinian-ring-finite-local-product] to write $H=\prod_iH_i$ with nonzero local Artinian factors. Each factor is finite-dimensional over $\Omega$. Its core $B_\Omega(H_i)$ is a field by [lem-sfb-ind-etale-core-ring-operations] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-idempotent-zero-one], and is finite-dimensional as a subspace of $H_i$. Therefore its structural embedding of $\Omega$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial]. The product assertion of [lem-sfb-ind-etale-core-ring-operations] consequently identifies the core inclusion with $\prod_i\Omega\longrightarrow\prod_iH_i$, componentwise the structural maps.

Each $H_i$ has exactly one prime by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime]. Its residue field is finite-dimensional over $\Omega$, hence equals $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial]. Thus there is exactly one $\Omega$-algebra homomorphism $H_i\to\Omega$: any such map has prime kernel, which must be the maximal ideal, and the induced map on the residue field must fix $\Omega$. A homomorphism from $\prod_iH_i$ to the field $\Omega$ selects exactly one factor, since precisely one of the orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$ maps to $1$. The same is true for $\prod_i\Omega$. Step 3 therefore shows that restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Omega\text{-alg}}(H,\Omega)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Omega\text{-alg}}(C\otimes_K\Omega,\Omega)$ is injective. For an arbitrary field $F$ and two ring maps $B\to F$ agreeing on $C$ (hence on $K\subseteq C$, so they are $K$-algebra maps for one $K$-structure on $F$), embed $F$ in an algebraic closure $\Omega$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The extended maps $H\to\Omega$, $b\otimes z\mapsto h(b)z$, agree on $C\otimes_K\Omega$ by the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Hence they agree, so the original maps agree. Every field-valued point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is of this form (or there are no points). The field-point criterion in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] proves that $v$ is universally injective, and that its diagonal is surjective.

source.place: Tag 01S4 (lemma-universally-injective), using more-algebra.tex Tag 0CKU and algebra.tex Tag 00KH; field-valued point argument

proof.text: The inclusion $C\subseteq B$ is integral: $B$ is finite as a $C$-module, since a finite $K$-spanning family still spans over $C$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] applies. Lying over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] proves that $v$ is surjective. This includes $C=B=0$, when surjectivity is empty. We have proved separately the three generic properties needed below: finite local freeness of $v$, surjectivity of $v$, and surjectivity of $\Delta_v$.

Order the nonzero elements $g$ of $R$ by divisibility (equivalently use their directed preorder); all upper bounds can be chosen as products and remain nonzero. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations], $K=\varinjlim_{g\ne0}R_g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $\operatorname{Spec}K=\varprojlim_{g\ne0}\operatorname{Spec}R_g$. These are small index categories, being formed from a set of elements of $R$. Descend the finite etale $K$-algebra $C$ using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-filtered-colimit-descent]: for some nonzero $g$, obtain an etale $R_g$-algebra $C_g$ and an identification $C_g\otimes_{R_g}K\cong C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], the etale morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}R_g$ makes $C_g$ a finitely presented $R_g$-algebra. Both $C_g$ and $A_g$ are finitely presented over $R_g$ (for $A_g$, localize the presentation from step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras](2), after replacing $g$ by a nonzero multiple, the inclusion $C\hookrightarrow B$ descends to an $R_g$-algebra homomorphism $h_g:C_g\to A_g$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies its generic map with $v$. Injectivity of $h_g$ is neither assumed nor needed.

source.place: Tags 01YX/01YW (directed inverse limits of schemes); algebra.tex Tags 00CR, 00U2(9), 05N9(2)

proof.text: For completeness the descended arrow has the finite-presentation hypothesis required by the descent lemmas. Put $R'=R_g$, and choose presentations $C_g=R'[t_1,\ldots,t_s]/(q_1,\ldots,q_a)$ and $A_g=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_b)$. Choose polynomials $P_i(x)$ representing $h_g(t_i)$. Then $A_g$ is the $C_g$-algebra $$C_g[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_b,t_1-P_1(x),\ldots,t_s-P_s(x)).$$ Indeed substitution of $t_i=P_i(x)$ recovers its given $R'$-presentation; each $q_j(P(x))$ already vanishes modulo the $r_k$ because $h_g$ is a homomorphism. Its diagonal is induced by $A_g\otimes_{C_g}A_g\to A_g$, multiplication, whose kernel is generated by the finitely many $x_i\otimes1-1\otimes x_i$: quotienting by these relations identifies the two copies of every polynomial in the generators. Thus this diagonal too is of finite presentation. All schemes in these two arrows, and the base, are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The same holds at every later localization.

source.place: Elementary generator-and-relation presentation calculation; algebra.tex Tag 05N9 context, and schemes.tex Tags 01I4/01JQ affine fibre-product formula

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] to $\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}R_g$, whose generic fibre is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] twice, to $u_g=\operatorname{Spec}h_g$ and its relative diagonal, using steps 4 and 5. In each application the base system is $\operatorname{Spec}R_h$ for nonzero multiples $h$ of $g$, with limit $\operatorname{Spec}K$; step 7 verifies the locally finite presentation and qcqs hypotheses. Take a common nonzero multiple of the finitely many indices. Finiteness persists under further localization, since a finite module generating family localizes to a generating family. Surjectivity, both for the arrow and for its diagonal, persists by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change]; the affine fibre-product formula identifies these further localizations with base changes. The structure map remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. Over this new initial stage apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to the base changes of $u_g$: its generic fibre is finite locally free by step 2, and step 7 still supplies finite presentation. Let $f$ be the resulting nonzero index. The preceding persistence arguments preserve finiteness and etaleness of the structure map and surjectivity of both $u_f$ and $\Delta_{u_f}$ at this final stage. Thus $u_f$ is finite locally free without requiring its rank to be constant.

Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}C_f$, let $u=\operatorname{Spec}h_f$, and let $e:T\to\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ be its structure morphism. The ring map $h_f$ is an $R_f$-algebra map, so contravariance gives exactly $e\circ u=p|_{D(f)}$; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its source with $E\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R_f$. Step 8 makes $e$ finite etale, $u$ finite locally free and surjective, and $\Delta_u$ surjective. By [def-weil-radicial-morphism], the last assertion makes $u$ universally injective. By [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft], $u$ is integral; [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism] therefore makes it a universal homeomorphism. The assertion about all base changes being bijective on points follows directly from the definition [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. No part of the argument required $E$ reduced, irreducible, or of positive rank.

source.place: Tags 01S4, 01WJ (lemma-finite-integral), 04DF (lemma-universal-homeomorphism); assembly of BLR 7.6 Proposition 5(a) generic factorization
